title: Slice Resampling and Tenant Fairness Manual (2025)
author: Maya Chen
content:
> **Archived 2026-01-10:** this page is superseded by "Slice Resampling, Cost-Fairness and Tenant Prioritization Manual" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

Purpose
This manual explains how Redwood refreshes and resamples evaluation probe slices while keeping compute cost, annotation spend and tenant fairness under control. Audience: evaluation engineers, probe-slice stewards, and the SRE/product partners who approve budgets.

Scope
- Covers recurring probe rotations and ad-hoc resampling for shadow evaluations, sentinel probes and monthly benchmark sweeps.
- Describes how resampling plugs into the eval harness probe scheduler and the annotation pipelines.
- Model promotion checklists remain in the model-onboarding docs.

Definitions
- Slice: a labeled prompt subset representing one workload slice (intent, language, long-context, ...).
- Resampling: drawing fresh probes from the candidate corpus to refresh or grow a slice.
- Priority Weight: a score between 0.1 and 10.0 used when splitting probe budget.
- Tenant Fairness: limits that stop any one customer-derived slice from absorbing too much annotation or evaluation budget.

Guiding Principles
1) Cost-aware: tag every resampling run with an estimated token/compute budget and get sign-off from the steward or budget owner.
2) Representative: probes should mirror production traffic plus a set of targeted edge cases.
3) Fair: per-tenant ceilings and soft quotas apply to high-volume tenants.
4) Traceable: seed lists, sampler configs and annotation batches are stored with provenance metadata.

Metrics and Signals
- Probe budget consumption (tokens, inference-seconds), expected vs actual. Alert at 10% deviation.
- Effective coverage delta: share of new probes adding new token sequences or intent tags. Target: >= 10% novelty for a refresh.
- Tenant budget share per window. Soft cap: 25% of monthly probe budget; hard cap: 40%.
- Annotation latency and cost per label. Target median <= 48 hours.

Resampling Policy
1) Trigger types
   a) Scheduled refresh: monthly automated refresh of high-impact slices.
   b) Drift-triggered refresh: fires when telemetry shows embedding drift > 0.08 or fidelity drop > 5%.
   c) Emergency expansion: on-call initiated resampling to capture a newly emerging pattern.
2) Budget pre-authorization
   - Every trigger needs an estimate of tokens, model runtime (seconds) and annotation seats.
   - Auto-approve thresholds: budgets under 50k tokens and inferred runtime < 1200s can be scheduled automatically. Anything larger goes to the slice steward and cost-owner.
3) Default sampling algorithm
   - Step 0: fingerprint the target distribution from the last 7 days of telemetry and compute stratified weights across language, intent and context-length buckets.
   - Step 1: allocate N probes per bucket proportionally, with a floor of 3 probes per bucket.
   - Step 2: within each bucket, mix 60% random production samples, 30% adversarial generator output, 10% human-curated edge cases.
   - Step 3: cap selection per tenant (see Fairness rules).
4) Novelty and deduplication
   - Exact token-sequence dedupe plus fuzzy canonicalization (whitespace, punctuation).
   - Drop candidates with cosine similarity > 0.95 to any probe from the last 180 days unless flagged high-priority.

Fairness and Tenant Prioritization Rules
- Soft quota: a tenant may not receive more than 25% of a slice's probes in a monthly window without stakeholder approval.
- Hard quota: 40% cap enforced automatically during sampling; violations open an ops ticket.
- Priority override: Sales or CSM may request a higher priority weight for onboarding customers with written approval and a cost offset plan.

Integration with Eval Harness
1) Write a sampler manifest (YAML) and attach it to the slice page. Required fields:

manifest.yaml:
---
slice_id: "intent-similarity-3"
owner: "nlp-probe-steward"
priority_weight: 2.5
budget_tokens: 80000
trigger_type: "drift"
fingerprint_window_days: 7
sampling_strategy:
  distribution: ["language","intent","context_bucket"]
  composition: {random: 0.6, adversarial: 0.3, human: 0.1}
annotation_policy: "tier-1"
---

2) Upload the manifest to the registry:
   - CLI: redwood-eval-manifest upload --file manifest.yaml --env shadow
   - CI: the eval-lint job validates schema and token budget.
3) The scheduler returns a plan (probe batch id, expected cost). Approve it if it falls within pre-authorization.

Annotation and Stewardship
- Tiers: tier-0 (auto-label), tier-1 (single human pass), tier-2 (double review). Default is tier-1.
- Annotator instructions include the anchor prompt, label schema, disagreement policy, redaction requirements and privacy gating.
- Retention: raw probes and annotator decisions kept 365 days; aggregates kept 5 years.

Rollout Checklist (before a resampled slice enters production evals)
1) Manifest registered and steward signoff.
2) Dry-run of N=50 probes through the harness on the production model variant.
3) Acceptance criteria:
   - Novelty >= 10%
   - Per-tenant share <= 25%
   - Expected cost within +/- 10% of budget
4) Run on the shadow mesh for 72 hours and collect telemetry.
5) Owner and product QA sign off.

Regression Triage Runbook
1) The owning steward opens a Regression-Triage ticket with the probe-batch-id and diffs.
2) Quick checks (5-15 minutes): dedupe/tokenization/canonicalization outputs, manifest vs execution, per-tenant caps.
3) If the regression persists, bisect the new batch (halves; random vs adversarial subsets).
4) If the adversarial generator is the cause, quarantine that sub-batch and rerun with extra human curation.
5) Post a status update to affected teams within 2 business hours.

Config Table (Operational Defaults)
| Field | Default | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| priority_weight | 1.0 | Range 0.1-10.0 |
| budget_tokens | 50000 | Override only with approval |
| fingerprint_window_days | 7 | Reduce to 1 for emergent issues |
| novelty_target_pct | 10% | Minimum novelty threshold |
| per_tenant_soft_cap | 25% | Monthly window |
| per_tenant_hard_cap | 40% | Enforced automatically |

Operational Commands
- Validate manifest: redwood-eval-manifest lint manifest.yaml
- Preview plan: redwood-eval-manifest preview --manifest manifest.yaml --n 50
- Force-run (on-call only): redwood-eval-manifest run --manifest manifest.yaml --env shadow --force
- Fetch provenance: redwood-probe-store fetch --batch-id <id> --format jsonl

Troubleshooting FAQ
Q: The resample went over budget.
A: Pause the batch and open a cost-variance ticket. Overages under 10% can be approved retroactively by the steward; larger ones need the budget owner.

Q: One tenant dominates the selected probes.
A: Quarantine the batch, roll back the slice and open a tenant-fairness incident.

Ownership and Contacts
- Steward: nlp-probe-steward (PagerDuty team: eval-stewards)
- Eval-harness integration lead: Alejandro Ortiz <alejandro@redwood.com>
- Cost escalation: Finance Ops (costops@redwood.com)

Change Log
- 2025-09-15: Initial draft of resampling policy.
- 2025-12-01: Added tenant soft/hard caps and auto-approve thresholds.

Note: quantization gating is not covered in this version; this page is deprecated in favor of the 2026 manual.

End of document.
